objective: Make the HolyAgent Pi extension recognise a T3 Code session, keep only the T3 tools HolyAgent uses, and warn when the thread runs below Full access.
scope: Worktree /home/user/holyagent-0.3.0-t3host, branch release/0.3.0/feat/pi-t3-host. Research to rely on (read both before starting): /home/user/holyagent/.git/holyagent/reports/assignment-0mw8td52p-27ab.md (Pi 1.5.0 extension API: ctx.mode, hasUI, RPC ui methods, session_tree, setActiveTools, trust, setModel) and /home/user/holyagent/.git/holyagent/reports/assignment-0mw8tdgpq-hfsl.md (T3 Code pi driver: T3_PI_RUNTIME_MODE, T3_MCP_URL, the mcp__t3-code__ tool names and mcp__t3_code__ hidden aliases, which ui requests T3 renders, the bridge extension re-adding tools in reconcileDiscovery).

T3 detection: a session runs under T3 when ctx.mode is rpc and the environment carries T3_PI_RUNTIME_MODE or T3_MCP_URL (T3 sets these when it injects its bridge). Put the detection in one small exported function so the docs and later work share it.

Tool filter (T3 Intent requirements 8, 9 and 13): under T3, the root keeps the T3 tools html_render, html_preview, preview_*, t3_preview_* and device_* and deactivates every other tool named mcp__t3-code__<name> or its hidden alias mcp__t3_code__<name> (orchestrator_capabilities, delegate_task, task_status, task_cancel, create_threads, t3_thread_*, schedule_task, list_scheduled_tasks, delete_scheduled_task, t3_pending_request and anything else outside the kept families). Compute the active set from pi.getAllTools() with the root tool selection the extension already applies (applyRootTools, rootActiveTools in packages/runtime/src/pi/tools.ts, T3_PREFIX), apply it once at session_start before the first request, and reapply the same set on before_agent_start and session_tree only when the active set has drifted (T3s bridge re-adds tools in its own handlers), so the provider tool list stays byte-stable for prompt caching. Add a tool_call block as backstop that refuses any deactivated T3 tool with a reason naming it, so a deferred tool reached through tool_search is refused too.

Full access: under T3, when T3_PI_RUNTIME_MODE is anything but full-access (approval-required or auto-accept-edits), deliver one warning that HolyAgent threads need T3 Full access because every extension tool call prompts and background specialists can stall, and how to switch. T3 drops notify outside an active turn, so deliver it through the notice path the extension already uses for its status message (delivered once on the next run) and also with ctx.ui.setStatus, which T3 shows near the composer.

RPC UI: under ctx.mode rpc the extension itself must call no ctx.ui.custom, setWidget, setFooter, setHeader, setTitle or theme methods; if it calls none today, add a test that pins this. Do not touch the rpiv packages here.
Plain pi terminal: none of this changes behaviour outside T3 (no T3 env): the filter is a no-op and no warning is shown.
